page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.m1.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the ecs.m1 family. It is built on the x86_64 CPU architecture and runs on the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 4 physical cores, meaning hyperthreading is disabled with exactly 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

This instance type does not include any bundled local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring users to attach external block storage volumes for operating system and application data. Additionally, there are no integrated graphics processing units or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this configuration.

An analysis of the CPU flags reveals that this instance lacks support for advanced instruction sets. It does not support Advanced Vector Extensions, Advanced Matrix Extensions, hardware-accelerated cryptography, or bit manipulation instructions. This absence of vector and matrix acceleration limits its efficiency for modern cryptographic operations, heavy mathematical computations, and machine learning workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.m1.medium offers a standard resource density profile for legacy or basic general-purpose workloads. Given the dedicated CPU cores but lack of modern instruction set extensions, this instance is appropriate for standard web serving, basic application hosting, lightweight database nodes, and general-purpose utility workloads that do not rely on vector-heavy processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.m1.medium is an x86_64 general-purpose instance within the ecs.m1 family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with no hyperthreading, alongside 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, necessitating external block storage for data persistence. A key hardware limitation is the lack of advanced CPU instruction sets, such as AVX, AVX512, AMX, and hardware-accelerated cryptography like AES. This resource profile makes the ecs.m1.medium qualitatively cost-efficient for legacy utility workloads, basic web serving, and lightweight application hosting, while rendering it unsuitable for vector-intensive computations or modern cryptographic tasks.
